sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Examination Content Outline - July 2026
keyFacts: People represents 33 percent of exam items.
Process represents 41 percent of exam items.
Business Environment represents 26 percent of exam items.
Approximately 40 percent of items use predictive approaches and the remaining 60 percent is divided between adaptive or agile and hybrid approaches.
The exam contains 180 questions, including 170 scored and 10 unscored pretest questions.
Candidates need at least 35 hours of qualifying project management training unless an applicable credit pathway applies.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted PMI publication. Cite and paraphrase. Use only short quotations when necessary. Do not reproduce tables, tasks, enablers, or proprietary exam content wholesale.

sources.title: Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification
keyFacts: Current eligibility pathways vary by educational background and generally require two to five years of non-overlapping project leadership experience within the prior ten years.
The current published exam experience is 180 questions in 240 minutes.
Third-party training may qualify, subject to PMI requirements and audit.
sources.usageLimitations: Current web content may change. Display retrieval date and direct learners to PMI for final eligibility decisions.

sources.title: What Is New in the Updated PMP Exam
keyFacts: The July 2026 refresh adds AI, sustainability, and stakeholder engagement to project-based scenarios.
The refreshed exam places greater emphasis on outcomes, value, and business impact.
PMI announced future restrictions for live training in late Q4 2026 while continuing to recognize qualifying self-paced training from third parties, subject to PMI rules.
sources.usageLimitations: Training rules are time sensitive. Verify again before publication and before making any eligibility claim.

sources.title: PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct and Ethics Guidelines
keyFacts: PMI identifies responsibility, respect, fairness, and honesty as core ethical values.
The current code is effective from 17 November 2025.
PMI members, volunteers, certification holders, and certification applicants are expected to comply with the code.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted content. Summarize and cite. Do not reproduce the full code without permission.

sources.title: Permissions and Trademark Use Guidance
keyFacts: Substantial reproduction or republication of PMI-owned content generally requires permission.
Use of PMI marks must not imply sponsorship, endorsement, authorization, or affiliation without permission.
The Obserra course must use original instruction and original practice questions.
sources.usageLimitations: Obserra must not use the PMI logo or official courseware without permission. Include an independence and trademark notice.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 Project, Programme and Portfolio Management - Guidance on Project Management
authoritativeFor: predictive incremental iterative adaptive and hybrid delivery
keyFacts: ISO 21502 applies across organization types and projects of different purposes, sizes, costs, durations, complexities, life cycles, and delivery approaches.
The standard recognizes predictive, incremental, iterative, adaptive, hybrid, and agile approaches.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted ISO standard. Use the public abstract and licensed access only. Paraphrase; do not reproduce clauses or tables without permission.

sources.title: ISO 21500:2021 Project, Programme and Portfolio Management - Context and Concepts
keyFacts: ISO 21500 describes organizational context and underlying concepts for project, programme, and portfolio management.
Its guidance is applicable across organization size, type, and project complexity.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted ISO standard. Paraphrase public abstract unless licensed.

sources.title: ISO 10006:2017 Quality Management - Guidelines for Quality Management in Projects
keyFacts: ISO 10006 gives guidance for applying quality management in projects of different sizes, durations, complexities, and sectors.
It distinguishes quality management in projects from general project management guidance.
sources.usageLimitations: Copyrighted ISO standard. Paraphrase public abstract unless licensed.

sources.title: GAO Schedule Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Project Schedules
keyFacts: GAO describes ten best practices for developing and maintaining a reliable high-quality schedule.
An integrated schedule can show whether major milestones and completion dates are realistic and achievable.
A reliable schedule can show how proposed changes affect the overall program.
sources.usageLimitations: U.S. government publication. Cite the report and verify any quoted passage against the official text.

sources.title: Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Developing and Managing Program Costs
keyFacts: GAO provides a consistent methodology for reliable and high-quality cost estimates.
The practices have been applied to spacecraft, software, communications networks, construction, rail, census, and other programs.
Reliable cost forecasts and updates support budgeting, oversight, and performance evaluation.
sources.usageLimitations: U.S. government publication. Cite report number and date.

sources.title: NASA: Assessments of Major Projects
keyFacts: NASA planned to invest about 74 billion dollars in major projects in fiscal year 2025.
Four of 18 major projects had cost overruns and three had schedule delays in the assessed year.
Three of 53 historical projects accounted for almost half of total overruns in GAO's analysis.
sources.usageLimitations: Use as a documented public case. Do not infer that one project management technique alone caused or would have prevented the reported outcomes.

sources.title: Space Station: Inadequate Planning and Design Led to Propulsion Module Project Failure
keyFacts: GAO reported that the initial project did not meet performance, cost, and schedule goals largely because fundamental planning and execution processes were not followed.
A subsequent assessment defined success criteria, identified design assumptions, and compared alternatives before recommending a design.
sources.usageLimitations: Historical government case. Explain context and avoid claiming direct equivalence to modern private-sector projects.

sources.title: PMI Publishes Global Standard for AI in Project Work
keyFacts: PMI's 2026 AI project-work standard addresses responsible AI governance from design through deployment.
The announcement identifies AI business cases, tool selection, risk management, ethics oversight, and compliance as project leadership concerns.
sources.usageLimitations: Use announcement-level facts only unless Obserra obtains the standard under an appropriate license.
